mainTopic: The end of the נקדימון story, valuing gold and local goods for the כתובה, and the minimum dowry for a bride or an orphan girl
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of נקדימון בן גוריון. The גמרא explains why his family lost its wealth even though he gave צדקה, and a ברייתא describes his daughter's terrible poverty. The גמרא then returns to the כתובה. רבי יוחנן rules that gold in a dowry is written at its exact value. Two ברייתות are brought against him, and the גמרא works through them, ending by reading 'gold is like utensils' as talking about broken gold or gold granules. Next comes a list of goods that count like money in particular places, and רבא explains why he changed his mind about the money pouches of מחוזא. A new משנה sets a minimum dowry of fifty זוז for a daughter or an orphan girl, and אביי proves these are small local coins. Finally a ברייתא teaches that an orphan girl is supported before an orphan boy, and a second case about the two orphans begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: But he gave so much charity!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a source showing that נקדימון בן גוריון was very generous with the poor. That makes it hard to understand why his family lost everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: Cloths were spread under him to walk on, and poor people came behind him and folded them up to keep.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a challenge that started on the previous page. The גמרא is pointing out that נקדימון בן גוריון clearly did give צדקה to the poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא said his family's wealth was lost because he did not give enough צדקה. This source shows the opposite, since poor people took the expensive cloths he walked on. So the earlier claim seems wrong.
steps.confusionAlert: This section starts in the middle of a sentence. The question began on the previous page: 'Didn't נקדימון בן גוריון give צדקה?'

phrases.english: they would spread out beneath him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is נקדימון בן גוריון: fine cloths were laid down for him to walk on. This sentence started on the previous page.

phrases.english: and poor people would come
and fold them up behind him!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַצִּיעִין תַּחְתָּיו, וּבָאִין עֲנִיִּים וּמְקַפְּלִין אוֹתָן מֵאַחֲרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a challenge that began before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that נקדימון בן גוריון lost his wealth because he did not give צדקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A source shows he let the poor take his expensive cloths, so he did give צדקה.

steps.title: First answer: he did it for his own honor
steps.stepSummary: Answer one: his giving was really about showing off, not true צדקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say that he did it for his own honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the challenge. The giving was done to make himself look important.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fact that the poor took the cloths is not denied. But because his goal was his own honor, it does not count as real צדקה that would protect his wealth.

keyTerms.meaning: if you wish, say (introduces a possible answer)

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
he did it for his own honor,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His letting the poor take the cloths was real צדקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was done for his own honor, so it does not count as the צדקה he was missing.

steps.title: Second answer: he gave less than he should have
steps.stepSummary: Answer two: he did give, but not as much as someone that rich was expected to give.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or say that he did not give as much as he should have. As people say: the load matches the camel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. He gave, but for a man of his huge wealth it was not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer accepts that his giving was sincere. The point is that how much a person must give depends on how much he has. A strong camel carries a heavy load, and a very rich man must give much more.

keyTerms.meaning: as was fitting for him / as he should have
as people say (introduces a common saying)
according to the camel is the load

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers about נקדימון: either his giving was for his own honor, or it was too little for a man as rich as he was.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
he did not do as much as he should have done.
As people say:
According to the camel is the load.
phrases.notes: A stronger camel is given a heavier load. In the same way, more is expected from a richer person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: כִּדְבָעֵי לֵיהּ לְמִיעְבַּד לָא עֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Measuring the amount against his wealth
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any generous giving should have been enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: What is expected depends on how rich a person is, and he gave less than that.

steps.title: The daughter gathering barley in עכו
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק swears that he saw נקדימון's daughter picking barley from between horses' hooves in עכו.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק said, 'May I not see the comfort of Israel if I did not see her gathering barley from between horses' hooves in עכו.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא describing how poor נקדימון's daughter became. An eyewitness tells what he saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her family was once extremely rich. Now she had to search for barley grains in the dirt among horses. He uses an oath to show this really happened.

keyTerms.meaning: may I see comfort (an oath formula)

phrases.english: It was taught:
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok said:
May I see the comfort,
phrases.notes: This is a way of swearing. He means: may I not see the comfort of Israel if this is not true.

phrases.english: if I did not see her
gathering barley
from between the hooves of horses in Akko.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק: אֶרְאֶה בְּנֶחָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of נקדימון's family
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An eyewitness tells that נקדימון's daughter fell into deep poverty.

steps.title: The פסוק he read about her
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק applies a פסוק from שיר השירים to her, reading 'your kids' as 'your bodies.'
steps.simpleTranslation: I read this פסוק about her: 'If you do not know, fairest among women, go out after the flock's footsteps and feed your kids.' Do not read 'your kids' but 'your bodies.'
steps.whatsHappening: He finishes his story by applying a פסוק to her situation. He changes how one word is read to make the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about following the flock and feeding young goats. By reading גדיותיך as גויותיך, it describes someone following animals to feed her own body. That is exactly what she was doing among the horses.

keyTerms.meaning: do not read it as ... but as

steps.whatToRemember: נקדימון's daughter fell from great wealth to picking barley among horses, and the פסוק is read as 'feed your bodies.'

phrases.english: I read this verse about her:
"If you do not know,
O fairest among women,
go out by the footsteps of the flock
and feed your young goats."
Do not read "your young goats,"
but rather "your bodies."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story of the daughter with a פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק is read as 'feed your bodies,' describing her following animals to find food.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: gold is valued at its true worth
steps.stepSummary: If a bride brings gold into the marriage, it is appraised and written in the כתובה at exactly its value.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמן בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If she brought him gold, it is appraised, and it is written at its value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the rules of writing the dowry into the כתובה. רבי יוחנן gives a rule for gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, cash in a dowry is written for more than its value, and goods are written for less. רבי יוחנן says gold is in neither group. It is written at exactly what it is worth, with nothing added and nothing taken off.

keyTerms.meaning: she brought in (as part of her dowry)

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the focus of the challenges that come next.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Shemen bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
If she brought him gold,
it is appraised,
and it counts at its actual value.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הִכְנִיסָה לוֹ זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the story to the laws of the כתובה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gold in a dowry is appraised and written at its exact value.

steps.title: A ברייתא says gold is like utensils
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says gold is treated like utensils, which seems to mean it is written for less, like silver vessels that wear down.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: Gold is like utensils. Doesn't that mean like silver utensils, which lose value?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן with a ברייתא. It suggests the ברייתא treats gold like other goods that are written for less.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silver vessels wear down with use, so they are written for less than their value. If gold is 'like utensils' in that sense, it would also be written for less. That goes against רבי יוחנן, who said its exact value.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Gold is like utensils.
Isn't it like silver utensils,
which lose value!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's rule
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that gold is written at its exact value
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If gold is like silver utensils that wear down, it should be written for less than its value.

steps.title: No, like gold utensils, which don't lose value
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means gold is like gold utensils, which do not wear down, so it stays at its true value.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, like gold utensils, which do not lose value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by reading the ברייתא another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gold does not wear down the way silver does. So if 'utensils' means gold utensils, they keep their value, and that fits רבי יוחנן's rule.

phrases.english: No, like gold utensils,
which do not lose value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading which utensils the ברייתא means
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Utensils' means silver utensils, which wear down.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Utensils' means gold utensils, which keep their value.

steps.title: Then it should have said 'like its own utensils'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that answer. If gold utensils were meant, the ברייתא should have said 'like its utensils.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should have said 'like its utensils'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 8, based on the ברייתא's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying gold is like gold utensils would be phrased 'like its own utensils.' The ברייתא said 'like utensils' in general, which sounds like ordinary utensils that wear down. So the challenge to רבי יוחנן returns.

phrases.english: If so,
it should have said "like its utensils"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'utensils' means gold utensils
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That meaning would have been worded 'like its utensils,' not 'like utensils.'

steps.title: Another ברייתא: gold, gold coins, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא: gold is like utensils, gold coins are like cash, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that where they are not exchanged, they are appraised at their value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, it was taught: Gold is like utensils. Gold dinars are like cash. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: In a place where people do not usually exchange them, they are appraised and count at their value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא to challenge רבי יוחנן. This step sets up the analysis that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has two parts: plain gold is like utensils, and gold coins are like cash, which is written for more. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that where these are not exchanged, they are valued at their exact worth. The question is which part he is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: to exchange them for smaller coins

phrases.english: And furthermore, it was taught:
Gold is like utensils.
Gold dinars are like cash.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
In a place where it is the custom not to exchange them,
they are appraised, and they count at their value.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, תַּנְיָא: זָהָב הֲרֵי הוּא כְּכֵלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge against רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that gold is written at its exact value
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא again calls gold 'like utensils.' The next steps work out what it means.

steps.title: Which part is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is talking about plain gold or about gold coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, which part is he talking about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the ברייתא. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His words could be about the first part (plain gold) or the last part (gold coins). Which one he means changes what the first תנא holds about gold.

keyTerms.meaning: on which one? (which part is he talking about)

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, which part is he talking about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to read the ברייתא just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is talking about plain gold or about gold coins

steps.title: It can't be about the gold coins
steps.stepSummary: If he were talking about gold coins, the first תנא would treat them as cash even where they are not used. That makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he is talking about the last part, then the first תנא holds that even where they are not exchanged they count as cash? But there they are not used!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבן שמעון בן גמליאל were talking about gold coins, the first תנא would be calling them cash even where nobody spends them. But money that cannot be spent cannot be treated like cash. So this option fails.

keyTerms.meaning: the first תנא (the unnamed opinion before the named one)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'לא נפקי' means the coins are not spent or used as money. It does not mean 'they do not go out' physically.

phrases.english: If you say he is talking about the last part,
phrases.notes: The last part is the line about gold dinars being like cash.

phrases.english: that would mean the first Tanna holds
that even in a place where it is the custom not to exchange them they are like cash?
But they are not used there!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא אַסֵּיפָא, מִכְּלָל דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to step 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is talking about the gold coins
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The first תנא would be treating coins as cash in a place where they are not even spent as money.

steps.title: If he meant plain gold, then gold equals silver utensils
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל must have been commenting on the first clause about plain gold. That forces the תנא קמא's 'utensils' to mean silver utensils, which contradicts the earlier answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't he commenting on the first part? Here is what the ברייתא means: gold is like utensils. Which utensils? Silver utensils. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: in a place where people don't usually spend gold, it is like gold coins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it started in steps 10-12. Since רבן שמעון בן גמליאל can't be talking about gold coins, he must be talking about plain gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says plain gold is 'like gold coins,' then the תנא קמא must have meant something different by 'utensils.' The only option is silver utensils. That directly contradicts step 8's answer that gold is like gold utensils.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it…? (introduces the forced conclusion of a challenge)
The first clause of a teaching
To exchange them / use them as spending money

phrases.english: Rather, is it not on the first clause,
phrases.notes: The first clause is the line about plain gold, not the line about gold coins.

phrases.english: and this is what it is saying:
gold is like utensils;
what utensils? Utensils of silver.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
it is like gold dinars,
in a place where they are accustomed not to exchange it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the forced conclusion after step 12 ruled out the gold-coins reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 8's answer that gold is like gold utensils.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבן שמעון בן גמליאל speaks about plain gold, the תנא קמא's 'utensils' must mean silver utensils, not gold ones.

steps.title: He was talking about coins that are hard to spend
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל really was talking about gold coins. The case is a place where the coins can be spent, but only with difficulty, and that is the point of the argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. He really is talking about the last part, the gold coins, in a place where people can spend them, but only with difficulty. Here is the argument: one opinion says that since they can be spent, we add to their value for her. The other says that since they can be spent only with difficulty, we don't add to their value for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the gold-coins reading by narrowing the case. These coins are not unusable; they are just hard to spend.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 rejected the gold-coins reading because the תנא קמא couldn't call unusable coins 'cash.' Now the case is coins that can be spent, but with effort. The תנא קמא treats them as cash, so they get the cash increase in the כתובה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says no increase. Plain gold can therefore still be like gold utensils.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause of a teaching
We increase the value for her, as with cash

steps.whyThisMatters: This rescues step 8's answer that gold is like gold utensils.

phrases.english: No, really it is on the last clause,
phrases.notes: The last clause is the line about gold coins.

phrases.english: and it is where they are used only with difficulty.
And this is what they disagree about:
one Sage holds: since they are used,
we increase it for her,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא נָפְקִי אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי הַדְּחָק,
phrases.english: and one Sage holds: since they are used only with difficulty,
we do not increase it for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 by reviving the reading that step 12 rejected, in a narrower case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (coins spendable only with difficulty)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Coins that aren't spent at all couldn't be called cash, so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל must be talking about plain gold.
steps.terutzMaskana: The coins can be spent with difficulty. The תנא קמא treats them as cash; רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not.

steps.title: The whole ברייתא is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's, with words missing
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: there is no argument at all. The ברייתא is missing words, and the entire teaching belongs to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: the whole thing is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's, and some words are missing. It should read: gold is like utensils, and gold coins are like cash. When? Where people usually spend them. But where people usually don't spend them, we appraise them, and they count at their real value. This is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view, as he says: where people usually don't spend them, we appraise them, and they count at their real value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different way out by filling in words it says are missing from the ברייתא. Now one speaker says it all, with no argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's line is not an argument against the first part. It adds a condition to it: gold coins count as cash only where people spend them. Plain gold stays 'like utensils,' so it can still mean gold utensils.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces another answer)
Some words are missing from the text

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל arguing with someone. In this answer, the whole ברייתא is his, and his line only adds a condition.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלַּהּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא,
phrases.english: the whole of it is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
and it is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
gold is like utensils,
gold dinars are like cash.
When is this said?
In a place where they are accustomed to exchange them.
But in a place where they are accustomed not to exchange them,
they appraise them, and they are at their value;
these are the words of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
For Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
in a place where they are accustomed not to exchange them,
they appraise them, and they are at their value.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: כּוּלַּהּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to the challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was arguing with the first part, which forced 'utensils' to mean silver utensils.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is all one opinion, and the condition about spending applies only to gold coins. Plain gold can still be like gold utensils.

steps.title: The wording problem still stands
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא is settled, but the original wording problem remains. If gold utensils were meant, it should have said 'like its utensils.' The גמרא calls this reading a difficulty, and the next steps answer by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either way, it should have said 'like its utensils'! This is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the wording challenge from step 9 and admits that reading 'utensils' as gold utensils does not work. This sets up a new answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 14-15 only answered the contradiction from the second ברייתא. Step 9's point still stands: plain 'like utensils' doesn't sound like 'its own utensils,' meaning gold ones. The word קשיא admits the gold-utensils reading has a real difficulty. The next step answers by reading the ברייתא a different way.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a difficulty (here it rejects one reading; the next step answers with a new one)

phrases.english: In any case,
it should have said "like its utensils"!
phrases.notes: This is the same wording question from step 9.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets aside the second ברייתא and goes back to the open wording challenge from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 8's reading that 'utensils' means gold utensils.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If gold utensils were meant, the ברייתא would have said 'like its utensils,' not just 'like utensils.'

steps.title: The ברייתא is about broken pieces of gold
steps.stepSummary: A new reading of the first ברייתא: it is talking about broken gold fragments. These are treated like ordinary utensils, not like coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: what case are we dealing with here? Broken pieces of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a fresh way to read 'gold is like utensils' that avoids the wording problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'utensils' simply means ordinary goods, so there is no need for the word 'its.' The new point is that broken gold is treated like goods to be appraised, not like gold coins.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
Broken or crushed pieces of gold

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
with what are we dealing here?
With broken gold pieces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gets around the unanswered wording problem by redefining what gold the ברייתא means.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Utensils' had to mean gold utensils, so the wording didn't fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about broken gold. It is like ordinary goods, not like coins, so the plain word 'utensils' fits.

steps.title: רב אשי: it is about gold granules
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a slightly different case: the ברייתא is about small grains of gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: it is about gold granules.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers his own version of the same kind of answer: a different form of raw gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like step 17, this reads 'gold' as unworked gold rather than coins or utensils. Granules are treated like goods, not cash. The only difference is which kind of raw gold is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Gold granules / small grains of gold

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's 'gold is like utensils' ends up read as raw gold, either broken pieces or granules. It is valued as goods, not like gold coins. The 'like its utensils' wording question was a קשיא only for the gold-utensils reading. Reading the ברייתא as raw gold avoids it.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: with granules.
phrases.notes: He means tiny grains of gold, not worked into anything yet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel version of step 17's answer, with granules instead of broken pieces.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was about gold utensils, and the wording didn't fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about gold granules, which are treated like ordinary goods.

steps.title: Spices in Antioch count as money
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי says that in Antioch, spices are treated like cash.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: Spices of Antioch are like money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a new teaching to the earlier topic of goods that are valued like money. רבי ינאי says that in Antioch, spices count as cash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Antioch people traded with spices the way others trade with coins. So spices there get the status of money, even though elsewhere they are ordinary goods.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a short list showing that 'money' depends on what a place actually uses for trade.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said:
Spices of Antioch
are like money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the earlier discussion of gold coins and fragments to a list of local goods that work like money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a place where spices are used for trade, they are treated like cash.

steps.title: Camels in Arabia can pay a כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says a woman can collect her כתובה from camels in Arabia.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Camels of Arabia, a woman can collect her כתובה from them.
steps.whatsHappening: Another item is added to the list. In Arabia, camels are so commonly used for trade that a woman can be paid her כתובה with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like spices in Antioch, camels in Arabia work like money there. So they can be used to pay what a woman is owed for her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: The כתובה payment owed to a woman

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Camels of Arabia —
a woman collects her כתובה from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel example to the spices of Antioch.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where camels are the normal means of trade, a woman may collect her כתובה from them.

steps.title: Robes in Bei Mikhsei can pay a כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי says robes in a place called Bei Mikhsei work like money for a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said: Those robes of Bei Mikhsei, a woman can collect her כתובה from them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי adds another local example to the list. In Bei Mikhsei, robes are used like money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Same idea again: what counts as payment depends on what people in that place actually trade with.

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said:
Those robes of Bei Mikhsei,
a woman collects her כתובה from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another example in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Robes in Bei Mikhsei count like money for collecting a כתובה.

steps.title: Sacks and ropes in certain towns can pay a כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי adds that sacks in Rodya and ropes in Kimchonya also work like money.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פפי said: These sacks of Rodya and ropes of Kimchonya, a woman can collect her כתובה from them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי gives two more local examples. In these towns, sacks and ropes are trade goods used like money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new in the reasoning; the list just grows. Each town has its own 'currency' goods.

phrases.english: And Rav Pappi said:
These sacks of Rodya
and ropes of Kimchonya —
a woman collects her כתובה from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same רב פפי, continuing the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sacks in Rodya and ropes in Kimchonya count like money for collecting a כתובה.

steps.title: רבא's first view about the money pouches of מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: רבא says he used to think a כתובה could be collected from the money pouches of מחוזא, because people there relied on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: At first I used to say: those money pouches of מחוזא, a woman can collect her כתובה from them. What is the reason? People rely on them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tells us what he used to think. He thought the money pouches in מחוזא were what people there depended on, like land elsewhere, so a כתובה could be collected from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a כתובה is backed by land, the thing people depend on for security. רבא thought that in מחוזא, people kept their wealth in money pouches instead, so those pouches filled the role of land. This step is only his earlier view; the next step tells us he changed his mind.

keyTerms.meaning: At first I used to say
Their reliance, what they depend on

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop here! This is רבא's old opinion, and he takes it back in the next step.

phrases.english: Rava said: At first I used to say:
Those money pouches of Mechoza —
a woman collects her כתובה from them.
What is the reason?
Their reliance is on them.
phrases.notes: He means the people of מחוזא depended on these pouches the way others depend on land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another possible item for the list, but presented as a view רבא once held.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא's earlier view: the pouches of מחוזא act like land, so a כתובה can be collected from them.

steps.title: רבא changes his mind: they really rely on land
steps.stepSummary: רבא saw that people spent the pouches to buy land, so he concluded their real security was land, not the pouches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once I saw that they take them and they get spent, and when they find land they buy it with them, I said: their reliance is on land.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why he dropped his earlier view. He saw that people used the pouches to buy land whenever they could.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the pouches were their real security, people would hold onto them. Since they spend them to buy land, it shows land is what they truly rely on. So the pouches do not take the place of land for a כתובה.
steps.whatToRemember: Goods count like money only where people really trade with them. רבא learned that the pouches of מחוזא were just a step toward buying land, so they do not replace land.

phrases.english: Once I saw that they take them and they go out,
phrases.notes: 'Go out' here means the pouches get spent and leave their hands.

phrases.english: and when they find land they buy it with them,
I said: their reliance is on land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא rejects his own earlier view from step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's earlier claim that the pouches of מחוזא act like land.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: People spend the pouches to buy land, which shows land, not the pouches, is their true security.

steps.title: משנה: A father must give at least fifty זוז
steps.stepSummary: A father who marries off his daughter without naming a dowry must give her at least fifty זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who marries off his daughter without specifying should not give her less than fifty זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. If a father did not say how much dowry he would give, he still must give at least fifty זוז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with no agreement, there is a basic minimum dowry. The father cannot send his daughter into marriage with nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: One who marries off (gives in marriage)

phrases.english: MISHNAH
One who marries off his daughter without specifying
should not give her less than fifty zuz.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on the topic of minimum dowry.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father who gives no dowry terms must give at least fifty זוז.

steps.title: משנה: The husband must clothe a 'bare' bride before the wedding
steps.stepSummary: If the father said he gives nothing, the husband must provide her clothing while she is still in her father's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stipulated to bring her in bare, the husband should not say, 'When I bring her into my house I will clothe her with my clothing.' Rather, he clothes her while she is still in her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a case where the father openly gives nothing. The husband cannot wait until after the wedding; he must give her clothing beforehand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when no dowry comes from her father, the bride should not arrive with nothing of her own. The husband provides the clothing ahead of time, so she enters the marriage already dressed.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Bare' does not mean literally unclothed; it means the father gives no dowry at all.

phrases.english: If he stipulated to bring her in bare,
the husband should not say,
"When I bring her into my house
I will clothe her with my clothing,"
rather, he clothes her while she is still in her father's house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from an unspecified dowry to a case where the father gives nothing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a bride brings no dowry, the husband must clothe her before she leaves her father's house.

steps.title: משנה: An orphan bride gets at least fifty זוז, and more if the fund allows
steps.stepSummary: Those who marry off an orphan girl must also give at least fifty זוז, and if the charity fund has more, they give according to her dignity.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise one who marries off an orphan girl should not give her less than fifty זוז. If there is money in the fund, they provide for her according to her dignity.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same fifty-זוז minimum to an orphan girl married off by the community. If the fund has enough, they give her more, fitting her honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The community takes the father's place. Fifty זוז is the minimum, and when the charity fund can afford it, the orphan gets a dowry that fits her standing.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה sets a minimum of fifty זוז for every bride, and for an orphan the charity fund gives more when it can.

phrases.english: And likewise one who marries off an orphan girl
should not give her less than fifty zuz.
If there is money in the fund,
they provide for her according to her dignity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the fifty-זוז rule from a father to the community marrying off an orphan.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An orphan bride gets at least fifty זוז, and more from the charity fund if it can afford it.

steps.title: אביי: The fifty זוז are small local coins
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the fifty זוז in the משנה are local coins worth much less than standard ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: אביי said: Fifty provincial זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with אביי explaining which 'זוז' the משנה means. He says it means the cheaper local coins, not full-value ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were two kinds of זוז: standard ones and smaller local ones worth much less. אביי says the minimum dowry is fifty of the small ones. His proof comes in the next step.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Abaye said:
Fifty provincial zuz.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה's 'fifty זוז'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fifty זוז of the משנה are low-value local coins.

steps.title: Proof from the charity fund clause
steps.stepSummary: If fifty full זוז were meant, what 'more' could the charity fund give? So the end of the משנה shows the coins must be small ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know? From the fact that the later clause teaches: If there is money in the fund, they provide for her according to her dignity. And we say: what is the 'fund'? רחבה said: the charity purse. And if you think it means fifty actual זוז, if there is money in the fund, how much would we give her?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי proves his point from the end of the משנה. The charity fund gives 'more' when it can, and that only makes sense if fifty זוז is a small amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רחבה explained that the 'fund' is the charity purse. Fifty full זוז is already a large sum for charity, so it would be hard to imagine giving even more. Therefore the base amount must be fifty small coins.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do we know?
The later part of the משנה
If it enters our mind, if you think

phrases.english: From where do we know?
From the fact that the later clause teaches:
If there is money in the fund,
they provide for her according to her dignity,
and we say: what is the 'fund'?
Rachava said: the charity purse.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתִּין חֲמִשִּׁים זוּזֵי מַמָּשׁ,
phrases.english: And if you think it means fifty actual zuz,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בַּכִּיס כַּמָּה יָהֲבִינַן לַהּ?
phrases.english: if there is money in the fund, how much would we give her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the proof for אביי's claim in step 28.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that the fifty זוז are small local coins.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the משנה, where the charity fund gives more 'according to her dignity', with רחבה's explanation that the 'fund' is the charity purse.

steps.title: Conclusion: the fifty זוז are local coins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the משנה means fifty low-value local זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: fifty provincial זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the proof. אביי's reading is confirmed: the minimum dowry is fifty small local coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the charity fund is expected to give more when it can, the base amount must be modest. So the fifty זוז are the cheaper local coins.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this, conclude from this

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's minimum dowry is fifty local זוז, a small sum, which is why the charity fund can add more for an orphan when it has the money.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
fifty provincial zuz.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof in step 29.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The fifty זוז of the משנה are low-value local coins.

steps.title: The orphan girl is supported before the orphan boy
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that when a יתום and a יתומה both come for support, the יתומה is supported first. A man can go door to door, but a woman does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: if an orphan boy and an orphan girl come to be supported by the charity fund, we support the girl first and then the boy. A man can go around to people's doors asking for help, but it is not a woman's way to do that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about who comes first when two orphans ask the צדקה fund for food and support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling gives an order of priority, not a choice between the two. Both orphans get support, but the girl goes first. The reason is practical: the boy has another way to get help by going door to door, and the girl does not, so her need is more pressing.

keyTerms.meaning: To be supported, meaning to receive food and basic needs from the צדקה fund
To go around to the doors, meaning to go door to door asking for charity

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a basic rule of priority in giving צדקה. The person with fewer other ways to get help comes first.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the boy gets nothing. He is still supported, just after the girl.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
An orphan boy and an orphan girl who came to be supported
We support the orphan girl
and afterward we support the orphan boy,
because for a man, it is his way
to go around to the doors,
but it is not a woman's way to go around.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יָתוֹם וִיתוֹמָה שֶׁבָּאוּ לְהִתְפַּרְנֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After discussing what the צדקה fund gives an orphan bride, the גמרא brings a related ברייתא about priority between orphans in support.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both ask for support, the יתומה is supported before the יתום, because a man can go door to door asking for help and a woman does not.

steps.title: Opening words of a second ruling about the two orphans
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins a new case about a יתום and a יתומה. The rest of the ruling comes in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: An orphan boy and an orphan girl...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The ברייתא is starting a second case about the same two orphans, and the ruling itself comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ruling was about food and support. These opening words bring the same pair back for a new question, which the text that follows will explain. For now, just note that a new case has begun.

keyTerms.meaning: An orphan boy and an orphan girl. These words open the next case in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: An orphan boy and an orphan girl

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a second case about the same pair of orphans.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the opening of the case appears here. The ruling follows in the next part of the text.
